summary.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q4 FY26 PAT rose 69.6% QoQ to ₹255 crore, NIM recovered to 9.05% and ROA to 1.81%, with credit cost down to 2.51%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential gains across margin, credit cost, opex and profit: NIM rose 43 bps QoQ to 9.05%, credit cost fell to 2.51% from 2.62%, and Opex-to-AUM dropped to 4.13%. PAT reached ₹255 crore (up 69.6% QoQ) and full-year PAT was ₹542 crore. Asset quality improved across Stages 1, 2 and 3, with GNPA at 1.44% and 6MoB30+ at 1.05%. Management reiterated ROA as its North Star metric and said it expects ROA to keep improving, while investments in AI, branches and technology continue. A ₹2,500 crore QIP in April 2026 lifted the pro-forma CAR to 20.74%.

segments.name: Prime personal loans (PL Prime)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate about ₹468 crore at end-March 2026; 33% of Q4 disbursements straight-through digital, up from 28% in Q3, with a target of 35-40%. Over 70% of customers have bureau scores of 750+.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: 400 gold branches operationalised as committed; Q4 disbursement about ₹819 crore; over 90% of branches in Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.

segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: 12,500+ retail outlets across 240 locations; target to at least double consumer durable customer count in FY27; peak month of over 54,000 cases.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursals about ₹125 crore in Q4, up about 18% QoQ; FY26 disbursements ₹1,000 crore; used CVs are 70%+ of volume.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Launched a year ago; over 22,000 files processed and about ₹900 crore disbursed cumulatively; around 500+ consultants and partners; instant sanction about 20% of sanctions.

segments.name: Six new businesses
segments.commentary: Contributed close to 24% of disbursements in Q4 vs 20% in Q3 FY26.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to keep improving; management says disbursement yield gains will gradually feed into portfolio yield.
Credit cost seen as fairly robust from here on; 6MoB30+ expected to stay range-bound and trend lower as gold and PL Prime grow in mix.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 35-40% with commensurate disbursements; management said it could be a notch better.
Opex-to-AUM targeted lower by end of FY27 than current levels, but expected to fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ with branch clustering and investment trajectory.
ROA expected to move strength-to-strength over the next few quarters; no intermediate ROA guidance given.
Fee income expected to show strength in FY27 but no numerical guidance given.
Customer service AI bot expected to reach 80-85% autonomous resolution over the next two quarters; three agentic funnel agents due in Q2 FY27 to lift digital loan conversion by over 15%.
capex_capacity: 400 gold branches operationalised by March 2026; future branch openings planned along similar lines to last year, with front-end investment and clustering causing QoQ opex swings.
Consumer durables onboarding exceeded the ~12,000-outlet plan for the start of the year; aim to at least double consumer durable customer count over FY27.
AI: 42 of 76 identified AI projects deployed, 34 under development; token consumption above 30 million per month, up more than 100x YoY.
Credit AI for underwriters lets PL headcount process 1.2x the volume; no new PL underwriters hired during FY26 growth.
Collections: tech-enabled collection system being built with decoupled collection vectors; bucket flow improved 2x vs prior year.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield at 15.96%, up 40 bps QoQ; management cited pricing power as a key driver of NIM recovery.
Management said disbursements may reach one-third of book this year, supporting NIM and ROA.
Business loans run at low-to-mid teens growth; pre-owned car loans also held to low teens; LAP growth strong, restricted to tickets above ₹50 lakh.
Management said it is not doing micro-LAPs and has no exposure to small-ticket LAP segments, and cited the Middle East conflict as a watch item but no current stress.
Stage 1 assets 97.5% (97.4% in Q3 FY26); Stage 2 1.1%; Stage 3 1.44%; provisioning coverage 49%.

qa_highlights.question: What are disbursement yield and book yield for the quarter, and is the geopolitical situation a risk to asset quality or provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited disbursement yield of 15.96% (up 40 bps QoQ) and said portfolio yield will catch up gradually. On the geopolitical question it said exposure is within risk tolerance, with stress testing done; LAP tickets are above ₹50 lakh, and gold and salaried-PL exposure are low-risk, so no risk was seen. Management is closely watching the environment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state level for 6MoB30+ at 1.05%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 6MoB30+ would be range-bound at current levels, with downward trend as gold loans and PL Prime grow in AUM share. GNPA was described as the lead indicator of credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance was given. Management expects fee income strength in FY27 from processing fees, insurance and cross-sell, with growth now more calibrated after the launch phase.

qa_highlights.question: Status of technology and AI journey?
qa_highlights.answer: PL Prime is about 30% digital of a ₹480-500 crore monthly-scale business and expected to rise to 30-40%. Business loan digitisation is planned in 6-9 months. AI projects are cutting manpower needs, with no new PL underwriters hired.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROA and FY27 disbursement and AUM plans?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA expected to keep improving over the next few quarters, with no interim guidance. FY27 AUM growth guided at 35-40% with commensurate disbursements. Opex-to-AUM expected lower by March 2027, with 10-25 bps QoQ swings.

qa_highlights.question: How will negative long-term ALM be bridged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹2,500 crore capital raise bridges the gap; the reply came from a speaker not on the management list.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and external-environment risk on the ~50% unsecured book; management says it is monitoring but sees no current risk.
Opex-to-AUM may fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ with branch openings, and fee income has no numerical guidance.
Credit cost sustainability: 6MoB30+ is 1.05% and GNPA 1.44%; lower credit cost depends on gold and PL Prime mix shift.
Execution of AI agent rollouts (customer service bot to 80-85% autonomous resolution; three agents due Q2 FY27) and cost-to-serve gains.
Long-term ALM gap management and funding cost (7.63%) after the QIP.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin, credit cost and ROA, with repeated claims of a structural turn. Cautious on the external environment: management said it is closely watching the geopolitical situation but sees no current portfolio risk. Vague on fee income and quarterly opex, giving no numerical guidance.
key_quotes: Our ROA has moved to 1.81% this quarter versus 1. 2% last quarter.
Among all our six vectors in my limited view, ROA, I would treat as our North Star metrics.
In Q4, 33% of disbursements were processed through a fully straight-through digital processing.
